original_title: VA Ends Transgender Healthcare for Veterans and Federal Employees Covering 11 Million People

existing.title: VA Ends Transgender Healthcare for Veterans and Federal Employees Covering 11 Million People
existing.description_short: VA Ends Transgender Healthcare for Veterans and Federal Employees Covering 11 Million People
existing.description_medium: In spring 2025, VA Secretary Doug Collins announced the Department of Veterans Affairs would phase out all gender-affirming care for new transgender patients, restricting the program to veterans already receiving hormone therapy. Simultaneously, a January 2025 policy change stripped gender-affirming care from the Federal Employee Health Benefits program covering 11 million people, with full elimination of grandfathered coverage scheduled for the following year. By May 2026, veterans, federal employees, and 18-year-olds classified by Trump as children were collectively blocked from accessing care their doctors prescribed.

original_title: DOJ Reversal Allows Seizure of Journalists' Phone Records and Testimony

existing.title: DOJ Reversal Allows Seizure of Journalists' Phone Records and Testimony
existing.description_short: DOJ Reversal Allows Seizure of Journalists' Phone Records and Testimony
existing.description_medium: On April 25, 2025, Attorney General Pam Bondi issued an internal memo rescinding Biden-era protections that had barred prosecutors from seizing reporters' phone records, emails, and compelling journalist testimony in leak investigations. The new policy explicitly allows subpoenas, court orders, and search warrants targeting news media. The memo indicated investigations could be launched not just for classified leaks but for disclosures that 'undermine' Trump administration policies — a far broader standard. Press freedom groups called it a landmark threat to investigative journalism and source protection.
